A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, four figures, and Appendices A–E. Content can be reliably matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Figure 3 reports original simulations using 10,000 particles to compare ULA and linearly tempered ULA on two-dimensional Gaussian distributions.

after.justification: Figure 3 retains the original 10,000-particle Gaussian sampling simulations. These remain empirical results despite being unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: The tempered Langevin dynamics, discrete sampler, and optimal schedule in Equations 9, 11, and 15 are unchanged. The added explanation of power tempering reexpresses an existing path without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic Gaussian and mixture examples, including the Gaussian sampling experiment in Figure 3 and mixture-path illustrations in Appendix E. No evaluation domain or task is added.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains the same ULA and linearly tempered ULA comparison. Figure 2 likewise retains the optimal, linear-tempering, and vanilla-Langevin bound comparisons.

E3.justification: Figure 3 retains KL versus iteration count, 10,000 particles, and zero-mean two-dimensional Gaussians with covariance diagonal entries 1 for the proposal and 10 for the target. No experimental protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The convergence-rate validation, intermediate-distribution multimodality example, and mode-mass redistribution illustrations are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or additional analytical case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the numerical illustrations. The retained particle count describes simulation size, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 retain identical plotted content and the same reported findings. There are no added measurements, changed simulation curves, or revised empirical rankings; the bound corrections are mathematical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Equation 12 restores the A'-weighted sum of schedule increments and corrects discretization indices from k to i; the corresponding summed recursion already appeared in v1's Appendix B.1, Equation 33. v2 also corrects the Fisher-divergence denominator and replaces Cauchy–Schwarz with Jensen's inequality in Lemma 21's proof. The main theorem set and proof strategies remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about convergence bounds, optimal schedules, degraded functional inequalities, and exponentially slow geometric tempering, including for well-conditioned targets.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly identifies the 'uniform' proposal with Lebesgue measure and explains how power tempering with positive initial temperature fits Equation 6 through a normalized proposal and rescaled schedule. This clarifies applicability; the existing interpretations and failure conditions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit repository URL to the already cited BlackJAX library reference. This is a limited addition of third-party code access information; it does not disclose the authors' simulation code or new implementation settings.

R1.justification: v2 retains all 82 earlier references and adds Durmus and Moulines (2016) for ULA convergence and Polyanskiy and Wu (2022) for divergence inequalities. The positioning relative to other tempering and sampling approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short background clarification, acknowledgements, and expanded author information, corrects wording and proof cross-references, and switches to author-year citations. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The document-wide conversion to ICLR formatting changes typeface, page geometry, headings, running headers, and title/author layout. Existing figures are resized and repositioned; Figure 3 moves from within Appendix C.3 to after Appendix D's introduction. Their plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 12 brings the main discrete-time bound into agreement with the summed recursion already present in Appendix B.1. Smaller definition and proof corrections, clearer treatment of uniform proposals, and additional supporting citations improve precision. These are useful localized repairs; the theoretical scope and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
